findings.title: Other getSubGroupsStream overloads still NPE when the group is deleted concurrently
findings.body: Only `getSubGroupsCount()` got a null check on `modelSupplier.get()`. The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` unguarded. `modelSupplier` resolves to `getGroupModel()`, which returns null when the group was removed after the cached entry was loaded. That is the same race this PR fixes for the count, so those paths will throw the same NPE. Anything that lists subgroups of a group being deleted concurrently, such as the subgroups endpoint or tree loading, remains exposed. The fix should be applied consistently, for example by returning `Stream.empty()` when the model is null.

findings.title: Returning null for subgroup count silently leaks a null into the representation
findings.body: When the group vanished, `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns null instead of a number. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` passes it straight to `representation.setSubGroupCount(...)`, so a deleted group can still be returned to the client with a null `subGroupCount`. Clients and any other caller that unboxes the Long may not expect null. A count of 0, or dropping the vanished group from the result, would be a safer contract. At minimum the Javadoc/contract for null should be documented.

findings.title: Concurrency test starts an unjoined thread and asserts before it has finished
findings.body: The reader thread is started with `new Thread(...).start()` and is never joined. After `deletedAll.set(true)` the test immediately asserts that `caughtExceptions` is empty. The reader may be mid-request at that point and add its exception after the assertion has already passed, so a regression can go undetected. The thread is also non-daemon and untracked, so it can outlive the test. The test also depends on timing: nothing forces a reader call to overlap a delete, so it may pass even without the fix. It should join the thread (or use an ExecutorService/Future) before asserting, and ideally create overlap deterministically.
